reasons.D: Closest movement: short plain declaratives with the odd fragment, concrete procedural order and an understated closing image; only the email/meeting quip and 'jam is excellent' break the author's unsmiling reserve.
reasons.C: Sentence rhythm is close (short, stepwise, 'Then the step'), but a rhetorical question, 'All of it' and 'I will not pretend otherwise' add a wry, reader-facing stance and pile fragments more thickly than the passage does.
reasons.B: Short sentences but more explaining and moralising ('a real risk to her', 'Not many jobs are that plain', 'the worst kind'), a more earnest, justifying stance than the author's bare statement of fact.
reasons.A: Long, clause-heavy reflective essay sentences with colons, abstractions ('dignity', 'small fixed points') and a commentating tone; furthest from the author's clipped, concrete plainness.
